To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
“The shared experiences of the effectiveness of a single pair of rowers’ joint action were shaped by interpersonal mechanical states.”
the shared experiences of a pair of expert individual athletes were shaped by the interpersonal mechanical states that emerged during the first joint practice.
shared experiences of effectiveness are shaped by interpersonal mechanical states, and that this relationship is not linear.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the joint action dynamics are regulated by the individuals, in order to understand the dynamics of social coupling.
the study of how individuals experience their joint action, and how these experiences emerge from the dynamics of their interpersonal mechanical coupling.
the dynamics of joint actions and their regulation in the context of sports.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the saliency (and accuracy) in shared experiences of effectiveness in the joint action of a pair of rowers is shaped by interpersonal mechanical states.
shared experiences of effectiveness are shaped by interpersonal mechanical states.
the shared experience of effectiveness of a pair of rowers in a race was shaped by interpersonal mechanical states.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the joint action of a pair of rowers in a race can be understood as a process of interpersonal coordination in which the rowers are continuously adjusting their actions to the mechanical properties of their boat, and that the salience of the experience of the joint action is shaped by the interpersonal mechanical states.
the shared experiences of effectiveness in joint action are shaped by the inter-personal mechanical states.
shared experiences of effectiveness in a pair activity are shaped by the inter-personal mechanical states of the crew, which are also shaped by the extra-personal mechanical states.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effectiveness of a joint action can be experienced in different manners by the participants, which can be explained by their interpersonal coordination dynamics.

the salient experience of the joint action was not a necessary condition for the joint action to be effective, but that the effectiveness of the joint action could be explained by a shared experience of effectiveness.
, when a pair of individual rowers are asked to practice a new joint action, the salient experiences of effectiveness are not necessarily shaped by the interpersonal mechanical states.
